summary.en: AND requires both questions to be true.
summary.bn: &&, || আর ! দিয়ে শর্ত জুড়ো এবং short-circuit কোন কাজ বাদ দেয় তা বোঝো।

notes: Logical operators and their short-circuit rules apply throughout C89 to C23. C17 needs no Boolean header for integer truth expressions. stdbool.h can provide more readable flag declarations.

examples.title: Check a marks interval
examples.explanationHtml: Both comparisons are true, so AND produces one. A mark below zero or above one hundred would fail one side. The expression describes a closed interval without using a mathematical chained comparison.

examples.title: Skip an unnecessary update
examples.explanationHtml: The left zero decides the false result. C never evaluates the prefix increment on the right. Both printed fields are zero. This demonstrates skipped execution rather than an increment whose result was discarded.

examples.title: Guard a division
examples.explanationHtml: Count is zero, so the first comparison fails. The division is skipped completely, leaving a safe result of zero. Switching the two operands would attempt the division before its guard.

practice.title: Attendance and marks
practice.statementHtml: Read attendance and mark, each 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print 1 when attendance is at least 75 and mark at least 40, otherwise 0; finish the line.

practice.title: Either room
practice.statementHtml: Read room 0 to 999. After the prompt Input: , print 1 for room 201 or 202, otherwise 0, and newline.

practice.title: Normalize absence
practice.statementHtml: Read present from -10 to 10. After the prompt Input: , print the logical NOT of present and newline.

practice.title: A protected quotient test
practice.statementHtml: Read total 0 to 100 and count 0 to 10. After the prompt Input: , print 1 if count is nonzero and the integer quotient exceeds 2, otherwise 0; end with newline.
hints: The divisor guard must be on the left.

options: When the left operand is false
quiz.explanation: A false left side already fixes the result at zero.

quiz.prompt: When does logical OR skip its right operand?
options: When the left operand is true
quiz.explanation: A true left side already makes the result one.
Negative five is nonzero and therefore true; NOT reverses it.

quiz.prompt: Which expression safely guards division by count?
quiz.explanation: AND checks the guard first and can skip division.

quiz.prompt: False AND skips the increment. Which count remains?
quiz.explanation: The right operand is never evaluated.

quiz.prompt: True OR skips its right operand. Which values appear?
quiz.explanation: The result normalizes to one and c stays two.

quiz.prompt: NOT is applied before AND. Which truth result is printed?
quiz.explanation: NOT zero is one, and both operands are true.

keyPoints.en: AND requires both questions to be true.
keyPoints.bn: && হলে দুই শর্তই সত্য হতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: OR accepts at least one true question.
keyPoints.bn: || হলে অন্তত একটি শর্ত সত্য হলেই চলে।

keyPoints.en: NOT turns zero into one and nonzero into zero.
Short-circuiting can skip the right operand.
keyPoints.bn: বাঁ দিকেই ফল জানা গেলে ডান দিক আর চলে না।

keyPoints.en: Put a safety guard before the operation it protects.
keyPoints.bn: ঝুঁকিপূর্ণ কাজের আগে তার নিরাপত্তার শর্ত লেখো।

examQuestions.question: Read total 0 to 100 and count 0 to 10. After Input: print 1 if count is nonzero and the integer quotient exceeds 2, otherwise 0; end with newline.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int total, count;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &total, &count) != 2 || total < 0 || total > 100 || count < 0 || count > 10) {
        return 1;
    }
    printf("%d\n", count != 0 && total / count > 2);
    return 0;
}

The divisor guard must be on the left.
